html:
A Burkinabe film director whose films of village life, above all Yaaba (1989) and Tilai (1990), won international fame; Tilai won the Grand Prix of the jury at Cannes.

He worked with local actors, in Moore and other local languages, and told simple stories with the look of folk tales. With the FESPACO festival in Ouagadougou, his work made Burkina Faso a centre of African cinema. He later made films for television and on the region's wars. His success inspired a generation of directors from French-speaking Africa. See also Ousmane Sembene and Burkina's people.
